summary: ICLR 2026 paper by Jenny Zhang et al. An open-ended self-improving agent that writes and modifies its own code, selecting from an archive of past versions. Raised SWE-bench from 20% to 50% via iterative self-modification and empirical evaluation.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — the core mechanism is agent self-modification of its own orchestration code, an explicit red-flag pattern (prompt self-evolution, RL training loops) in AgentForge's curation rules. No verified gap it closes; sequential determinism is a deliberate design choice.

summary: April 2025 preprint by Robeyns et al. Removes the split between meta-agent and target agent; a single agent edits its own codebase to improve cost, speed, and benchmark performance.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — same category as DGM: self-modifying agent loop. AgentForge explicitly defers self-evolution patterns. DGM supersedes this as the stronger 2026 result.

summary: March 2026 preprint describing a six-phase autonomous development loop with automated drift control and human pause gates for long-running agent workflows.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the pause-gate concept (similar to AwaitingPlanApproval) and drift-control idea are interesting for AgentForge's state machine. However, no code repo found and the full paper wasn't accessible to verify details. Too thin to propose an issue from.

source: Accumulated Behavioral Rules for Coding Agents (arXiv:2607.13091)
summary: July 2026 paper proposing a closed-loop framework where every accepted code-review comment is codified as a persistent behavioral rule injected into future agent prompts. Prevents agents from repeating past review mistakes.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses the known gap that executor prompts don't receive distilled skills yet (Phase 2, limitation #8). Maps to AgentForge's existing distillation infrastructure (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). Backlog was full (11 issues) this run so no issue was created.

source: PROJECTMEM: Local-First Event-Sourced Memory for AI Coding Agents (arXiv:2606.12329)
summary: June 2026 preprint by Malo & Qiu (U. Utah). Append-only event log of typed events (issues, attempts, fixes) with a deterministic gate that warns agents before they repeat a failed fix or touch a fragile file. Exposed via MCP. PyPI package: projectmem.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the cross-run episodic memory concept is covered by open issue HID-188. The deterministic warning gate (don't repeat failed fixes) is a genuinely new angle not in HID-188, but the backlog is full this run.

summary: Benchmark released November 12, 2026 by Mercor. 26 long-horizon engineering and research tasks spanning software engineering, ML, and scientific computing. Uses continuous scoring rather than pass/fail. Claude Fable 5.2 leads at 54.6%.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — this is a benchmark for evaluating agents, not an orchestration pattern. AgentForge is an orchestration system, not a benchmark target. No actionable gap identified.

summary: 2026 LangGraph ecosystem additions: MongoDBStore and langgraph-oracledb for persistent cross-session memory. LangMem extends the store with semantic, episodic, and procedural memory types. Agent files stored as Hub commits for versioning.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already ships cross-run skill memory (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). The remaining gap (executor not receiving skills) is tracked by HID-188. These integrations don't map to AgentForge's CLI-subprocess model.

source: LangGraph deepagents v0.7.0 — timeouts and error recovery
summary: deepagents v0.7.0 adds finer-grained control over node execution including timeouts, error recovery, and graceful shutdown. Also reduces checkpoint overhead for long-running threads.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — automatic retry and failure classification is already tracked by open issue HID-167. No new gap identified beyond what that issue covers.

source: Karpathy Autoresearch — autonomous self-improving agent loop
summary: Karpathy's March 2026 Autoresearch project: an autonomous loop where agents run experiments to improve LLMs, accumulating 66k GitHub stars. Karpathy reports coding almost entirely via agents since December 2025.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Autoresearch is a self-improving RL loop, an explicit red-flag pattern. The broader signal (agent-first coding workflows are maturing) is already embodied in AgentForge's design.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework (AutoGen successor, GA April 2026)
summary: Microsoft placed AutoGen into maintenance mode in February 2026 and released Microsoft Agent Framework (Semantic Kernel + AutoGen merged) in GA on April 3, 2026. AutoGen is maintained for security and bug fixes only.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses Claude Code and Codex CLI subprocesses, not AutoGen/Semantic Kernel APIs. Framework consolidation doesn't require AgentForge changes.

source: MemCoder — cross-run memory transfer for coding agents (arXiv:2603.13258)
summary: March 2026 preprint describing abstracted cross-run memory for coding agents. Reports 3.7% average improvement via cross-domain memory transfer; finds raw execution traces are less suitable than abstracted insights for transfer.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the finding that abstracted insights transfer better than raw logs is relevant to how AgentForge's distillation prompts summarise runs. Skill distillation is already shipped; the specific insight (summarise, don't verbatim) is worth considering for HID-188 scope. Backlog full this run.
